dedupe_keys.name: kpler formerly spire maritime global ais ship tracking data

description: The maritime AIS business formerly sold as Spire Maritime is now presented on spire.com's maritime pages as ship tracking with Kpler. It supplies Automatic Identification System (AIS) vessel positions from a network that Kpler says it owns and operates, not relying mostly on third-party sources. Coverage: global, from coast to deep ocean; more than 300,000 vessels tracked daily from over 13,000 AIS receivers in 190 countries, combining a proprietary constellation of low Earth orbit satellites (satellite AIS with latency under one minute), roaming AIS from partner fleets on open-ocean routes and congested lanes, and a terrestrial network of over 6,600 proprietary and partner stations for busy ports; stated average message frequency 25 seconds, average data latency 5 seconds and a 5-minute average refresh across vessels. Format and access: commercial data feeds and platforms, with demos on request; uses named include berth management and congestion prediction for port authorities, routing and fuel planning for fleet managers, ETAs for commodity traders and sanctions and insurance monitoring. Licence: commercial; not read. Caveats: delivery formats, APIs, archive depth and prices were not read; the performance figures are the vendor's. Simulation uses: vessel positions and port calls for maritime network flow, port capacity planning and disruption (chokepoint closure) scenarios. Related records: Norway's open AIS stream (data-kystverket-open-real-time-ais-norway), Clarksons fleet data (data-clarksons-research-shipping-fleet-offshore-data) and Spire Global aviation and weather data (data-spire-global-satellite-ads-b-aviation-and-weather-data).
